findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_dialog_layout.mjs across the full roster (36 of 43 registry targets graded). The prover opens each view through the shared dialog_targets registry and measures every EFFECTIVE tap target's own box at 390px against this platform's 44px floor. EVERY ONE OF THESE FIXES WAS RE-MEASURED RATHER THAN TRUSTED, and that mattered: three of the five failed silently on the first attempt, each for a different reason (see this row's own note). A CSS edit that looks right and a CSS edit that takes are different facts. MEASURED FAILING: 175 effective tap targets under the floor - and unlike every other failure in this sweep, this one is NOT a styling oversight and was deliberately left unfixed. The offenders are .wilo-day-header cells at 39.3 x 51.4: tall enough, too NARROW. They are 39.3px wide because seven day columns share a 390px viewport, so the constraint is the GRID, not a padding value. Forcing 44px width means changing the grid - and the same prover, in the same run, also grades horizontal overflow at 390 (which this view currently PASSES, selfOverflow 0). Widening the columns to satisfy the touch floor risks failing the overflow oracle instead. Trading one measured oracle for another is not a fix, and doing it silently would be worse. THE REAL OPTIONS, which are design calls rather than edits: (a) make the week grid horizontally scrollable so columns can take their natural width; (b) show fewer days at 390px and page between them; (c) accept the WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 SPACING exception - these targets are 39.3 x 51.4 with no overlap, comfortably clearing the 24x24 minimum that standard actually sets, and this platform's 44px floor is its own stricter rule. Recorded for Ian rather than decided here.

findings.title: THE V2 SUBJECT IS UNREACHABLE, AND THE REASON IS A DEFECT ON THIS PAGE - not a limitation of the probe. Clicking the page's own '+ Schedule' control (the element carrying onclick="openAddModal()") leaves #modal with computed **visibility: hidden** at both 390 and 1280 CSS px, so nothing appears. Zer
findings.detail: THE V2 SUBJECT IS UNREACHABLE, AND THE REASON IS A DEFECT ON THIS PAGE - not a limitation of the probe. Clicking the page's own '+ Schedule' control (the element carrying onclick="openAddModal()") leaves #modal with computed **visibility: hidden** at both 390 and 1280 CSS px, so nothing appears. Zero console errors and zero page errors, so nothing threw: the open path runs to completion and still produces an invisible dialog. THE MECHANISM, READ FROM THE CASCADE ITSELF rather than inferred. Two rules govern it: `.sheet-overlay:not(.open), .modal-overlay:not(.open) { visibility: hidden; transition: opacity 0.25s, visibility linear 0.25s; }` and `.sheet-overlay.open, .modal-overlay.open { visibility: visible; transition-delay: 0s; }`. Visibility is therefore gated on an **`.open`** class. After the click, #modal's className is exactly `"modal-overlay"` - the `hidden` class has been removed and `display` has become `flex`, but `.open` is NEVER ADDED. There is no inline style. So the element has layout (measured 367x1275, with #modal-box at 367x569) and is invisible. IT IS A CONTRACT MISMATCH, WHICH IS WHY IT IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN PATCHING: the page's opener uses the OLD protocol - remove `.hidden`, set `display` - while the SHARED overlay CSS moved to an `.open` protocol. Pages whose openers were updated still work: inventory's #part-modal and logbook's #asset-modal both opened and were fully measurable in this same pass, and community's #thread-overlay and project-manager's #modal-wizard likewise. dayplanner was left behind. WHAT IT COSTS A PERSON: '+ Schedule' is the primary way to add an item to a day plan. The button responds, the page does not change, and there is no error - the most confusing possible failure, because nothing tells the user to try something else. Any other page using `.modal-overlay` with an un-migrated opener has the same bug, so the fix should be verified across every `.modal-overlay` / `.sheet-overlay` opener rather than only here. NOT MEASURED, DELIBERATELY: this row's own oracle (the V2 layout/state/visual contract) cannot be measured while the view cannot be reached, and a pass over an invisible dialog would be a false green - the exact shape this bank refuses. The row therefore stays OWED with the blocker named, and becomes measurable the moment the opener adds `.open`. TO FINISH (batched per A15, and it is one line): have openAddModal() add the `open` class to #modal - or better, route it through whatever shared helper the migrated pages use, so the next CSS contract change does not strand it again. Then walk dayplanner's V2 rows.

findings.detail: THE V2 SUBJECT IS UNREACHABLE, AND THE REASON IS A DEFECT ON THIS PAGE - not a limitation of the probe. Clicking the page's own '+ Schedule' control (the element carrying onclick="openAddModal()") leaves #modal with computed **visibility: hidden** at both 390 and 1280 CSS px, so nothing appears. Zero console errors and zero page errors, so nothing threw: the open path runs to completion and still produces an invisible dialog. THE MECHANISM, READ FROM THE CASCADE ITSELF rather than inferred. Two rules govern it: `.sheet-overlay:not(.open), .modal-overlay:not(.open) { visibility: hidden; transition: opacity 0.25s, visibility linear 0.25s; }` and `.sheet-overlay.open, .modal-overlay.open { visibility: visible; transition-delay: 0s; }`. Visibility is therefore gated on an **`.open`** class. After the click, #modal's className is exactly `"modal-overlay"` - the `hidden` class has been removed and `display` has become `flex`, but `.open` is NEVER ADDED. There is no inline style. So the element has layout (measured 367x1275, with #modal-box at 367x569) and is invisible. IT IS A CONTRACT MISMATCH, WHICH IS WHY IT IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN PATCHING: the page's opener uses the OLD protocol - remove `.hidden`, set `display` - while the SHARED overlay CSS moved to an `.open` protocol. Pages whose openers were updated still work: inventory's #part-modal and logbook's #asset-modal both opened and were fully measurable in this same pass, and community's #thread-overlay and project-manager's #modal-wizard likewise. dayplanner was left behind. WHAT IT COSTS A PERSON: '+ Schedule' is the primary way to add an item to a day plan. The button responds, the page does not change, and there is no error - the most confusing possible failure, because nothing tells the user to try something else. Any other page using `.modal-overlay` with an un-migrated opener has the same bug, so the fix should be verified across every `.modal-overlay` / `.sheet-overlay` opener rather than only here. NOT MEASURED, DELIBERATELY: this row's own oracle (the V2 layout/state/visual contract) cannot be measured while the view cannot be reached, and a pass over an invisible dialog would be a false green - the exact shape this bank refuses. The row therefore stays OWED with the blocker named, and becomes measurable the moment the opener adds `.open`. TO FINISH (batched per A15, and it is one line): have openAddModal() add the `open` class to #modal - or better, route it through whatever shared helper the migrated pages use, so the next CSS contract change does not strand it again. Then walk dayplanner's V2 rows.

WHAT THIS ORACLE IS REALLY FOR, and the good news first: it checks that a refusal names PERMISSION rather than ID
findings.detail: FAILS: with 10 of this page's reads answered 403/42501, it says NOTHING AT ALL - the body text is 934 characters before the refusal and 992 after, and no new sentence explains anything.  WHAT THIS ORACLE IS REALLY FOR, and the good news first: it checks that a refusal names PERMISSION rather than IDENTITY, because this platform has already shipped that exact inversion - a 42501 rendered as 'your session has expired', which sends a signed-IN person to re-authenticate for a problem authentication cannot fix, and 401/403 collapsed into one message so neither audience got a true statement. ZERO of the 16 graded pages made that mistake on this run. utils.js:1607 whIsAuthFailure() is why: it returns FALSE for status 403 with the comment 'authenticated, and refused. Not a session problem', and documents 42501 as insufficient_privilege. That discrimination is holding. HOW THE REFUSAL WAS INDUCED, and why it is the real branch: every Supabase REST read is answered with the body PostgREST actually sends for a row-level-security refusal - HTTP 403 with {"code":"42501","message":"permission denied for table"} - so the page's own error handling takes the same path it would in production. The patch is on window.fetch, NOT page.route, because a warm service worker serves from cache and bypasses route interception; it is installed with addInitScript in a context closed after each page so it cannot leak. NON-WRITING: it makes a READ return 403. THE INJECTION PROVES ITSELF: every intercepted call increments a counter, and a page where the counter is zero is UNGRADED rather than judged. That guard exists because the first version of this prover silently did nothing - a regex written inside a template literal collapsed to one that terminates at its second character, so the init script was a SyntaxError, every read succeeded normally, and the prover reported 'the reads were all refused and the page said nothing' while nothing had been refused at all. Hit counts on this run ranged from 8 to 42 per page. AND THE SIGNAL MUST APPEAR: the same page is read WITHOUT the injection first, and if its ordinary copy already matches the refusal vocabulary the page is UNGRADED - which is exactly what happened to skillmatrix, whose normal text contains a matching phrase. Without that control a page whose everyday copy happens to say 'cannot' would pass for free. THE SYNTHESIS - THIS IS ONE MISSING SURFACE, NOT 15 PAGE BUGS. Of 16 graded pages: 13 said NOTHING AT ALL when every read was refused, 2 showed only a GENERIC error ('Analysis failed, check console'; 'Achievements failed to load.'), and 1 passed. The platform already has the pieces - a central WRITE-failure message and the correct 401-vs-403 discriminator in utils.js - but there is no equivalent on the READ path, so a refused read renders as dashes or blanks with no explanation. On logbook the numbers '516 entries 30 machines 6 open' became '- entries - machines - open' with the body text identical to the character (1107 before and after) and not one word about why. A person cannot tell 'there is no data' from 'the load failed' from 'you are not allowed', and those three call for three different actions. THE FIX IS ONE ADOPTION, not 15 edits: give the read path the same treatment the write path already has. This independently reproduces a finding already recorded as 'the message already exists; the gap is ADOPTION on the read path'. SCOPE: V1, the page as it loads, and READ refusal only - a refused WRITE is a different path with its own central message, and is not claimed here. 5 of the 22 pages are excluded from the sweep because they are public or have no authenticated read to refuse. The walk is NON-WRITING.

findings.detail: THE V2 SUBJECT IS UNREACHABLE, AND THE REASON IS A DEFECT ON THIS PAGE - not a limitation of the probe. Clicking the page's own '+ Schedule' control (the element carrying onclick="openAddModal()") leaves #modal with computed **visibility: hidden** at both 390 and 1280 CSS px, so nothing appears. Zero console errors and zero page errors, so nothing threw: the open path runs to completion and still produces an invisible dialog. THE MECHANISM, READ FROM THE CASCADE ITSELF rather than inferred. Two rules govern it: `.sheet-overlay:not(.open), .modal-overlay:not(.open) { visibility: hidden; transition: opacity 0.25s, visibility linear 0.25s; }` and `.sheet-overlay.open, .modal-overlay.open { visibility: visible; transition-delay: 0s; }`. Visibility is therefore gated on an **`.open`** class. After the click, #modal's className is exactly `"modal-overlay"` - the `hidden` class has been removed and `display` has become `flex`, but `.open` is NEVER ADDED. There is no inline style. So the element has layout (measured 367x1275, with #modal-box at 367x569) and is invisible. IT IS A CONTRACT MISMATCH, WHICH IS WHY IT IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN PATCHING: the page's opener uses the OLD protocol - remove `.hidden`, set `display` - while the SHARED overlay CSS moved to an `.open` protocol. Pages whose openers were updated still work: inventory's #part-modal and logbook's #asset-modal both opened and were fully measurable in this same pass, and community's #thread-overlay and project-manager's #modal-wizard likewise. dayplanner was left behind. NOT MEASURED, DELIBERATELY: this row's own oracle (the V2 layout/state/visual contract) cannot be measured while the view cannot be reached, and a pass over an invisible dialog would be a false green - the exact shape this bank refuses. evidence.checked: LIVE WALK. The confirmation read: 'week slot probe saved -> on your 2026-08-17 plan, and it syncs once you are back online.' It names the effect (the item joins that day's plan), the DAY it lands on, and the offline-sync condition. Reached as a person reaches it, and distinctly from V1: switchView('wilo') with the switch PROVEN (#logo-view == 'Week') because both views paint into the same #calendar-wrap, then the first visible per-slot 'Add task on <day> at <hour>' control. Those slots are [role=button] divs, not <button> elements - a finder that queried only 'button' reported a grid with 24 slots per day as having none, and polled for 12s against the wrong selector before I checked what the elements actually are. FOUND AND FIXED WHILE WALKING THIS VIEW - the slot's LABEL named a different day than the slot's VALUE. Measured: a slot announcing 'Add task on Sun, Aug 16 at 12 AM' opened the modal on 2026-08-17. The hour was carried correctly (12 AM -> 00:00); only the day disagreed, which is the hardest kind of wrong to notice on a planner. Root cause: one cell read by two clocks. toYMD() builds the stored value from LOCAL date parts (getFullYear/getMonth/getDate) and is what schedule_items.date is matched against, while whFmtDate() renders in a FIXED timeZone 'Asia/Manila' - so for any browser not in Manila the two disagree whenever local midnight lands on a different Manila calendar day. onSlotClick and openAddModal were both innocent: the slot passes its ymd and the modal honours it. Fixed by anchoring every label to Manila-midnight OF THE SAME ymd (new Date(ymd + 'T00:00:00+08:00')), which is exact for any local zone and changes nothing about what is stored; applied to the slot labels AND the week period header, which had the identical defect. Re-measured: the slot now reads 'Add task on Mon, Aug 17 at 12 AM' and the modal opens on 2026-08-17.

findings.title: FAILS: 42 of 42 number(s) rendered in #calendar-wrap carry no label a person could read beside them - "26" .milo-date; "27" .milo-date; "28" .milo-date; "29" .milo-date; "30" .milo-date.  HOW THE NUMBER-LABEL TEST WORKS AT DIALOG SCOPE, and why it is NOT the V1 rule: V1 walks up to 4 ancestors and a
findings.detail: FAILS: 42 of 42 number(s) rendered in #calendar-wrap carry no label a person could read beside them - "26" .milo-date; "27" .milo-date; "28" .milo-date; "29" .milo-date; "30" .milo-date.  HOW THE NUMBER-LABEL TEST WORKS AT DIALOG SCOPE, and why it is NOT the V1 rule: V1 walks up to 4 ancestors and accepts any subtree text under 400 characters. On a full page that discriminates; inside a DIALOG it cannot, because a dialog's whole subtree is usually under 400 characters, so the top ancestor 'labels' every number beneath it. The prover's own non-vacuity control PROVED that by failing - a bare 4242 injected into an opened dialog came back LABELLED - and the fix was to tighten the oracle, not to loosen the control, which would have been the exact inversion of its job. A label must now be PROXIMATE, which is what a person actually reads: the number's own aria-label/title, an associated <label for>, a parent aria-label, or text sitting beside it in a SMALL wrapper (<= 3 element children, <= 120 chars). THE CONTROL RUNS THE SAME PREDICATE as the oracle - a control that tests a different rule than the thing it validates proves nothing - and its probe is appended directly to the dialog, which has many element children, so the small-wrapper branch cannot fire and the probe has the shape of a genuinely unlabelled number. Every row below was banked only from a run where that control CAUGHT its injected number. HOW IT WAS MEASURED, and why these rows sat owed for so long: CJ was measured platform-wide at V1 and banked there, and V2/V3 stayed owed for ONE reason - nobody could open those views. Resolving all 15 dialog open paths (each read from SOURCE, never matched by label) removed that blocker, and the same measurements now run inside the OPENED dialog. The open-path table lives in tools/dialog_targets.mjs, shared with the modal-exit prover so the two cannot drift apart. SCOPED TO THE DIALOG, NOT THE PAGE, which is the whole point: a dialog OVERLAYS the page, so measuring document.body with a sheet open would re-measure V1 and bank it as V2 - the one-reading-for-every-layer error this bank has already paid for once. Every measurement is rooted at the dialog element. Overflow compares each visible descendant's right edge against the dialog's own content box, with a 1px tolerance (an earlier arc counted a 0.109px abutment as occlusion) and honours overflow-x auto/scroll/hidden/clip on an ancestor INSIDE the dialog, because a deliberately scrollable panel is not a defect. THE TAP-TARGET RULE IS PORTED VERBATIM FROM THE V1 PROVER, NOT REINVENTED, and that correction is why this number means anything. The first cut omitted four of V1's exclusions - sr-only, disabled, the actionable check, and the WCAG 2.5.5 inline-link-in-prose exception - and REPLACED a control's rect with its label instead of UNIONING them. Applying a stricter standard at V2 than at V1 does not find defects, it manufactures a difference between the two views and calls it one. With V1's exact rule restored the count came back IDENTICAL, which is what makes these findings real rather than an artifact: they are measured on the same ruler that banked 750/750 at page level. SCOPE: overflow is measured at THREE widths - 390, 641 and 1280 - and each width's row is banked from its OWN reading, never spread from one width to the others. The dialog is not closed between widths; two animation frames are awaited after each resize so the panel has actually reflowed, and a zero width at ANY width fails the whole target rather than quietly trusting the rest. TAP TARGETS are measured at 390 only - that is the mobile-first floor the V1 prover used, and a control that clears 44px at 390 does not shrink as the viewport grows. Two of the 15 dialogs are UNGRADED with their reason recorded rather than counted: resume's #review-sheet has no read-only path in (it needs the upload -> resume-extract pipeline, which WRITES) and hive's #handover-sheet cannot be reached at all. The walk is NON-WRITING - it opens a dialog, measures, and presses Escape.

findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing. THE JOURNEY: type into a composer, get called away, come back - and nothing may have half-landed. It is the most ordinary thing that happens to someone on a plant floor, and the failure it hunts is a page that treats abandoned input as a committed record. ★THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MAKES THE VERDICT FAIR, and without which this oracle would punish good behaviour: after the reload the marker text is looked for in TWO places, and they mean opposite things. Back inside the COMPOSER FIELD means a DRAFT was deliberately preserved - that is good UX and passes. Out in the page's own CONTENT means it half-landed, and a person who typed and walked away now owns a record they never submitted - that fails. A checker that merely searched the page for the text would call the good case and the bad case the same thing. NON-WRITING BY CONSTRUCTION: nothing is ever submitted; the marker only ever reaches an input's value, so this prover cannot pollute the shared test database. The composer inventory comes from tools/dialog_targets.mjs - the same grounded registry four other provers read - so which views count as composers cannot drift from how those views are known to open.FOR THIS PAGE AND PERSONA THERE IS NOTHING TO ABANDON. The prover walked all 66 (page, persona) pairs and reached a composer on 16 of them; this pair reported no composer at all, so the journey could not be CONSTRUCTED. ★THAT IS RECORDED AS UNBUILT, NOT AS A PASS, and the distinction is the whole point: a journey that cannot be constructed must never be scored green, because 'nothing half-landed' is trivially true of a surface where nothing can be typed. The prover carries that rail explicitly - non-vacuity, a journey that cannot be built is a finding rather than a quiet skip - and banking it green would be the empty-denominator failure this bank exists to catch. WHY THIS PAIR HAS NONE: the composer inventory is tools/dialog_targets.mjs, and a composer is only counted when it is reachable FOR THIS IDENTITY. index's fields, for instance, live on the anon landing and the sign-in modal, so a signed-in persona has no composer on that page even though the page plainly contains inputs. A read-only surface (public-feed, achievements, the report pages) has none for any persona. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: either this pair genuinely has a composer the registry does not yet list - in which case the registry gains an entry and the prover reaches it - or the row is dispositioned declared-na under R10 with 'this surface has nothing to abandon' as the reason and the page's own CO recovery oracles as the replacement. Left owed rather than declared here, because deciding which of those two it is needs the per-page composer question answered, not assumed.

findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs - 66 persona-journeys attempted across the roster.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs - 66 persona-journeys attempted across the roster. ★AND FIFTY OF THEM ARE NOT FINDINGS: they read 'journey could not be constructed: browser.newContext: Target page, context or browser has been closed', which is the harness dying mid-run, not a page failing a person. The run was killed twice - once by my own 570-second timeout and once when the backgrounded process lost its browser - and BOTH times it emitted those as FAILs. A probe whose browser is shot out from under it reports every remaining page as broken. ★SO THEY ARE NOT BANKED. Fifty false reds would have read as the worst finding of the session, and the only thing separating them from a real one is that I read the verdict string instead of the count. This is the same discipline as refusing a zero from a request counter a service worker was bypassing: an instrument that has stopped working reports the world as broken. ★WHAT IS BANKED IS THE SIXTEEN THAT ACTUALLY WALKED, plus the sub-journeys that completed: two_sided 15 walked / 0 failing, handoff 14 walked / 0 failing, abandon 7 walked / 1 failing. Those are real readings of a live product. FOR THIS PAGE: every journey attempt died with the harness, so nothing was measured here. Recorded as UNWALKED, never as failing - the difference between 'this page failed a person' and 'my browser closed' is the whole value of this row. ★RE-WALKED AFTER THIS SESSION'S TWELVE PRODUCT FIXES so the evidence carries digests of the code as it now stands. Re-WALKED, never re-baselined.

findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing. THE JOURNEY: type into a composer, get called away, come back - and nothing may have half-landed. It is the most ordinary thing that happens to someone on a plant floor, and the failure it hunts is a page that treats abandoned input as a committed record. ★THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MAKES THE VERDICT FAIR, and without which this oracle would punish good behaviour: after the reload the marker text is looked for in TWO places, and they mean opposite things. Back inside the COMPOSER FIELD means a DRAFT was deliberately preserved - that is good UX and passes. Out in the page's own CONTENT means it half-landed, and a person who typed and walked away now owns a record they never submitted - that fails. A checker that merely searched the page for the text would call the good case and the bad case the same thing. NON-WRITING BY CONSTRUCTION: nothing is ever submitted; the marker only ever reaches an input's value, so this prover cannot pollute the shared test database. The composer inventory comes from tools/dialog_targets.mjs - the same grounded registry four other provers read - so which views count as composers cannot drift from how those views are known to open.FOR THIS PAGE AND PERSONA THERE IS NOTHING TO ABANDON. The prover walked all 66 (page, persona) pairs and reached a composer on 16 of them; this pair reported no composer at all, so the journey could not be CONSTRUCTED. ★THAT IS RECORDED AS UNBUILT, NOT AS A PASS, and the distinction is the whole point: a journey that cannot be constructed must never be scored green, because 'nothing half-landed' is trivially true of a surface where nothing can be typed. The prover carries that rail explicitly - non-vacuity, a journey that cannot be built is a finding rather than a quiet skip - and banking it green would be the empty-denominator failure this bank exists to catch. WHY THIS PAIR HAS NONE: the composer inventory is tools/dialog_targets.mjs, and a composer is only counted when it is reachable FOR THIS IDENTITY. index's fields, for instance, live on the anon landing and the sign-in modal, so a signed-in persona has no composer on that page even though the page plainly contains inputs. A read-only surface (public-feed, achievements, the report pages) has none for any persona. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: either this pair genuinely has a composer the registry does not yet list - in which case the registry gains an entry and the prover reaches it - or the row is dispositioned declared-na under R10 with 'this surface has nothing to abandon' as the reason and the page's own CO recovery oracles as the replacement. Left owed rather than declared here, because deciding which of those two it is needs the per-page composer question answered, not assumed.

evidence.asserts: abandoning midway and returning leaves no half-applied state
evidence.checked: MEASURED with tools/prove_abandon_resume.mjs - the capture surface is opened, filled with a marker only this run could produce, and then ABANDONED BY RELOAD. Pressing a modal's X is CANCELLING, which pages handle deliberately; a reload is what actually happens when someone takes a call or their phone dies, and it is the one path no confirm dialog can intercept. ★THREE SHAPES ARE CHECKED SEPARATELY because each needs a different fix: a ROW THAT SHOULD NOT EXIST (psql, against this run's marker); a DRAFT THAT DOES NOT SAY IT IS A DRAFT (fields return pre-filled with no label, so the person cannot tell whether their work was SAVED or merely REMEMBERED); and a QUEUED WRITE that drains later. A restored draft is the GOOD design - it is judged on whether the surface LABELS it, never on whether it restores. ★AND THE PROBE PROVES ITS OWN FILL LANDED, so a green cannot be vacuous: an unfilled form makes 'no half-applied state' trivially true. My first logbook case invented an opener and a field that do not exist and came back UNGRADED rather than passing on an empty fill; the real controls were then read from tools/dialog_targets.mjs and the pages' own ids.  FOR THIS PAGE: a planned item, abandoned mid-add. Filled, abandoned by reload, and on return: 0 row(s) created, 0 field(s) pre-filled - no row was written and nothing came back pre-filled - a clean slate

evidence.asserts: a second press on Save cannot create a second schedule item
evidence.checked: LIVE WALK with every mutating request counted and HELD. Pressed Save twice 120ms apart: write count 1, the second press fired no further write, and the surface showed it - the control became unreachable. Reached as a person reaches it, and distinctly from V1: switchView('wilo') with the switch PROVEN (#logo-view == 'Week') because both views paint into the same #calendar-wrap, then the first visible per-slot 'Add task on <day> at <hour>' control. Those slots are [role=button] divs, not <button> elements - a finder that queried only 'button' reported a grid with 24 slots per day as having none, and polled for 12s against the wrong selector before I checked what the elements actually are. FOUND AND FIXED WHILE WALKING THIS VIEW - the slot's LABEL named a different day than the slot's VALUE. Measured: a slot announcing 'Add task on Sun, Aug 16 at 12 AM' opened the modal on 2026-08-17. The hour was carried correctly (12 AM -> 00:00); only the day disagreed, which is the hardest kind of wrong to notice on a planner. Root cause: one cell read by two clocks. toYMD() builds the stored value from LOCAL date parts (getFullYear/getMonth/getDate) and is what schedule_items.date is matched against, while whFmtDate() renders in a FIXED timeZone 'Asia/Manila' - so for any browser not in Manila the two disagree whenever local midnight lands on a different Manila calendar day. onSlotClick and openAddModal were both innocent: the slot passes its ymd and the modal honours it. Fixed by anchoring every label to Manila-midnight OF THE SAME ymd (new Date(ymd + 'T00:00:00+08:00')), which is exact for any local zone and changes nothing about what is stored; applied to the slot labels AND the week period header, which had the identical defect. Re-measured: the slot now reads 'Add task on Mon, Aug 17 at 12 AM' and the modal opens on 2026-08-17.

scenarios.question: mistakes, reversals and interruption - and after a slow tap: did my thing land?
scenarios.oracle: after a slow action the person can tell whether it landed, without guessing

evidence.asserts: after acting, the person is told whether it landed
evidence.checked: MEASURED with tools/prove_did_it_land.mjs: 26 controls driven, 26 pass, 0 fail, 0 ungraded - and NO WRITE REACHED THE DATABASE, every mutating request intercepted and answered in-page. ★THE QUESTION IS THE ONE A PERSON ASKS WITH THEIR THUMB STILL ON THE SCREEN: did that land? A surface that takes a press and says nothing leaves them to guess, and the guess is almost always 'do it again' - which is how a duplicate gets created. So the oracle is not 'did the write succeed' but 'was the person TOLD', and the two come apart exactly when the network is slow. ★AND IT IS ANSWERED BY ACTING, WHICH IS WHY THE INTERCEPTION MATTERS MORE THAN THE VERDICT. Every other check in this bank can be answered by looking; this one presses real controls on a live product. The requests are counted and answered inside the page so the probe cannot perform the thing it means to observe - a discipline this platform bought the hard way, when an earlier sweep hunting for a refusal ACTIVATED A SUCCESS because its filter excluded delete/pay but not save/generate. FOR THIS PAGE: 1 control(s) pressed. Each one told the person the outcome rather than leaving them to infer it. ★RE-WALKED AFTER THIS SESSION'S TWELVE PRODUCT FIXES so the evidence carries digests of the code as it now stands - R4b expired the prior rows because the fixes changed the functions they rested on. Re-WALKED, never re-baselined.

evidence.asserts: this view has no committing control, so there is no second press that could write twice
evidence.checked: NOT APPLICABLE: the month view has no action to press twice. MEASURED IN THE MONTH VIEW ITSELF and scoped to the container it renders into. Both the week and month views paint into the SAME element, #calendar-wrap, so the reach does not assume the switch happened - it calls switchView('milo') and then PROVES it took by checking that #logo-view reads 'Month', because a silently ignored switch would enumerate the week grid and file the reading against this view. Scoped there, ZERO visible enabled editable controls and ZERO commit-shaped controls were found at 390x844 as the supervisor, shared chrome excluded by name. The month grid is a roll-up you read to see where the work sits; the week view by contrast carries per-slot 'Add task on ...' buttons, which is exactly why these two views are graded separately rather than sharing one reading. Recorded declared-na rather than green (a pass over an empty denominator, which R10 forbids) or failed (which would invent an action). EXPIRES if the month view ever gains a control.
